newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends up, ACCESS climbs after AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends up, ACCESS climbs after AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, helped by technical buying after the recent sharp slide, ended higher across the board Thursday in sluggish trade, then gained more on ACCESS after a supportive AGA stock report.
February rallied 13.3 cents to close at $2.89 per million British thermal units, then climbed to $2.955 on ACCESS. March settled 14.2 cents higher at $2.623. Others also ended up.

"We couldn't break through the $2.61 low despite a weak Midwest physical market and the (mild) forecast. You had to get some sort of bounce after losing more than a dollar over the last week," said one Midwest trader.

AGA said Thursday that U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 128 bcf, more than most expected, and were just 54 bcf, or 2.5 percent, below year-ago. Stocks in the critical Consuming region east were 151 bcf, or 13 percent, above last year.
Technically, traders still saw resistance in February in the $2.96 area, with further selling likely at the $3.595-3.61 gap and then at the contract high of $4.02. Support was seen in the $2.60 area.
The National Weather Service is calling for above-normal temperatures across the U.S. for the next few days, with mild weather continuing into next week for the eastern U.S.

In the cash, January Gulf Coast prices were talked up slightly Thursday to about the $2.50 level. Midcontinent prices tumbled 60 cents to about $2.30. January gas in New York slipped 10 cents or more to the $3.50s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip rallied 13.3 cents to $2.356. NYMEX said 28,680 contracts traded, up from Tuesday's revised tally of 19,813.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas futures did not trade Thursday.

On the KCBT, February closed up 23 cents at $2.71, while deferreds finished 10 to 16.5 cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 9.7 cents to 18.0 cents (NYMEX premium). ((J Silha, New York Power Desk 212-859-1624))
